identity.title: Anaphylaxis signs: urticaria/flushing, angioedema, stridor, wheeze (NIAID/FAAN criteria)

technique.how: Look for acute (minutes to hours) skin/mucosal signs (generalised urticaria, flushing, pruritus, lip/tongue/uvula swelling) and pair them with respiratory compromise (stridor, wheeze, hypoxaemia) or hypotension/end-organ dysfunction; with a known allergen, two organ systems (adding persistent GI symptoms) or hypotension alone suffice. Apply the NIAID/FAAN criteria explicitly.
technique.prerequisites: Timeline of exposure and onset; blood pressure, SpO2 and airway assessment obtained simultaneously.
technique.contraindications: None. Give intramuscular epinephrine as soon as criteria are met; do not wait for full examination.

interpretation.positive_finding: Meeting NIAID/FAAN criteria identifies allergist-adjudicated anaphylaxis with sensitivity 95-97% and LR+ about 3-5 in ED validation cohorts; treat as anaphylaxis and give epinephrine.
interpretation.negative_finding: Not meeting the criteria makes anaphylaxis unlikely (LR- 0.04-0.07, NPV 96-98%), but 3-5% of adjudicated cases were missed, mostly presentations without skin findings.
interpretation.pitfalls: Skin signs are absent in a minority of anaphylaxis cases (especially with hypotension-predominant or drug/venom triggers), and antihistamines or beta-blockers blunt the picture. Isolated urticaria without a second system is not anaphylaxis.
interpretation.changes_what: Criteria met: IM epinephrine, remove trigger, monitor. Not met: pursue asthma, angioedema (ACE-inhibitor), sepsis, vasovagal or other causes but re-examine as symptoms evolve.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: anaphylaxis (allergist-adjudicated); finding = NIAID/FAAN clinical criteria met (any of the three criterion sets)
estimates.population: 214 ED patients coded as allergic reaction/anaphylaxis or related diagnoses, retrospective chart review, single US academic ED, Apr-Oct 2008
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis by two blinded attending allergists reviewing the record (kappa 0.77)
estimates.quote: sensitivity, 96.7% (95% CI, 88.8% to 99.1%); specificity, 82.4% (95% CI, 75.5% to 87.6%) … positive likelihood ratio, 5.48; and negative likelihood ratio, 0.04.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: anaphylaxis (allergist-adjudicated); finding = NIAID/FAAN clinical criteria met, prospective application
estimates.population: 174 prospectively enrolled ED patients seeking care for an allergic reaction/possible anaphylaxis, single US academic ED, 2010-2013
estimates.reference_standard: Independent blinded diagnosis by two board-certified allergist-immunologists (kappa 0.7)
estimates.quote: sensitivity, 95.1% (85.4%-98.7%); specificity, 70.8% (61.4%-78.8%) … positive likelihood ratio, 3.26; and negative likelihood ratio, 0.07.

sources.citation: Campbell RL, Hagan JB, Manivannan V, Decker WW, Kanthala AR, Bellolio MF, Smith VD, Li JT. Evaluation of NIAID/FAAN criteria for the diagnosis of anaphylaxis in emergency department patients. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.

Loprinzi Brauer CE, Motosue MS, Li JT, Hagan JB, Bellolio MF, Lee S, Campbell RL. Prospective validation of the NIAID/FAAN criteria for emergency department diagnosis of anaphylaxis. J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract. 2017.

Sampson HA, Muñoz-Furlong A, Campbell RL, Adkinson NF, Bock SA, Branum A, Brown SG, Camargo CA, et al. Second symposium on the definition and management of anaphylaxis: summary report. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2006.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not withhold epinephrine because criteria are 'not quite met' in a patient with rapidly progressive airway swelling or hypotension after a plausible exposure.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Stridor, hypoxaemia, hypotension or any sign of upper-airway swelling: give IM epinephrine immediately and prepare for airway management; biphasic reactions can follow hours later.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Allergist interrater agreement for the reference diagnosis: κ = 0.77 (Campbell 2012, Abstract) and κ = 0.7 (Loprinzi Brauer 2017, Abstract). No kappa for individual bedside signs located.

extraction_notes: Both estimates evaluate the NIAID/FAAN criteria as a whole (the id title names these criteria), so target_condition is prefixed COMPOSITE; no per-sign accuracy (urticaria, angioedema, stridor, wheeze individually) was found in these cohorts' abstracts. Prevalence computed from abstracts: 61/214 = 0.285 (Campbell) and 61/174 = 0.351 (Loprinzi Brauer). Same institution (Mayo Clinic) for both cohorts; the prospective cohort had lower specificity (70.8% vs 82.4%). LR CIs not reported in either abstract. Sampson 2006 cited for the criteria definition (consensus).
